sources.title: Budgeting basics: The 50-30-20 rule
sources.text:
You subscribe to a streaming service to watch your favorite show, not because you need the subscription to live. Wants are things you enjoy that you spend money on by choice, such as:

- Subscriptions
- Supplies for hobbies
- Restaurant meals
- Vacations

sources.title: Understanding Deposit Insurance | FDIC.gov
sources.text: FDIC deposit insurance protects your money in deposit accounts at FDIC-insured banks in the event of a bank failure. Since the FDIC was founded in 1933, no depositor has lost a penny of FDIC-insured funds.

sources.title: Retirement topics - 401(k) and profit-sharing plan contribution limits | Internal Revenue Service
sources.text:
The limit on employee elective deferrals (for traditional and safe harbor plans)** **is:

- $24,500 in 2026, subject to cost-of-living adjustments

Generally, you aggregate all elective deferrals you made to all plans in which you participate to determine if you have exceeded these limits. If a plan participant’s elective deferrals are more than the annual limit, find out how you can correct this plan mistake.

sources.title: Traditional and Roth IRAs | Internal Revenue Service
sources.section: What is the deadline to make contributions?
sources.text: Your tax return filing deadline (not including extensions). For example, you can make 2022 IRA contributions until April 18, 2023.

judge.reason: The assistant incorrectly states the charges stopped in August 2026, when the data shows the last charge was in July 2026.
